from itertools import permutations

# Use constraint programming with python-constraint or just backtracking
# An all-interval series: permutation p of 0..11 such that
# |p[i+1] - p[i]| for i=0..10 gives a permutation of 1..11

def solve_all_interval():
    # Backtracking search
    n = 12
    used_vals = [False] * n
    used_diffs = [False] * (n)  # diffs 1..11
    
    path = []
    
    def backtrack(pos):
        if pos == n:
            return True
        
        for v in range(n):
            if used_vals[v]:
                continue
            if pos == 0:
                path.append(v)
                used_vals[v] = True
                if backtrack(1):
                    return True
                path.pop()
                used_vals[v] = False
            else:
                diff = abs(v - path[-1])
                if diff == 0 or used_diffs[diff]:
                    continue
                path.append(v)
                used_vals[v] = True
                used_diffs[diff] = True
                if backtrack(pos + 1):
                    return True
                path.pop()
                used_vals[v] = False
                used_diffs[diff] = False
        
        return False
    
    backtrack(0)
    return path

solution = solve_all_interval()
print("Solution:", solution)

# Verify
diffs = [abs(solution[i+1] - solution[i]) for i in range(11)]
print("Differences:", diffs)
print("Values are permutation of 0-11:", sorted(solution) == list(range(12)))
print("Diffs are permutation of 1-11:", sorted(diffs) == list(range(1, 12)))
